title: Disentangling contributions of visual information and interaction history in the formation of graphical conventions
venue: Proceedings of the 41st Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society
one_sentence: 把 convention formation 从 verbal communication 推向 graphical communication；与你的 visual convention 路线直接相连。
problem: graphical meaning 可来自 resemblance 或 shared history，既有工作未分离 repeated-item learning、task practice 与 visual recognizability。
method: 138 AMT participants/69 dyads，固定 sketcher/viewer；4 repeated ShapeNet chairs×8 次、4 control chairs pre/post。245 naive recognizers，223 retained，比较 yoked same-sketcher sequence 与 shuffled sequence；mixed models、BIS 与 VGG-19 similarity。
findings: repeated objects 的 efficiency/accuracy improvement 大于 controls；yoked recognition improvement 大于 shuffled，stroke count 下降。
drawings 偏离各自初始形式、within interaction 更一致，并在不同 interactions 间适度分化。
real_contribution: 用 repeated/control 与 yoked/shuffled history controls 建立后来 C6 的核心方法骨架。
biggest_weakness: yoked observers 不是原 partner；manipulation 隔离的是 same-producer sequence continuity，不是 reciprocal common ground。单一 chair category、固定角色，部分结果在 C6 replication 中修正。
claim_boundary: 不能据此声称 arbitrary symbols、mutual negotiation、internal shared belief 或 embodied AI；C5 是 C6 明示的早期 findings subset，不应计为独立 evidence source。
why_researcher_should_care: 把 convention formation 从 verbal communication 推向 graphical communication；与你的 visual convention 路线直接相连。
